chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
The jealousy of a woman is heresy, and the jealousy of a man is belief.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a man's and a woman's jealousy in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the nature of jealousy (ghayrah) in men and women, categorizing the woman's jealousy as a form of kufr (disbelief/heresy) and the man's as iman (faith/belief). This hadith highlights a theological and ethical distinction in gender roles regarding possessiveness and exclusivity in relationships. In Shia scholarly tradition, this is often interpreted not as a denial of women's inherent worth, but as a reflection of the different spiritual and social responsibilities assigned to each gender, where male ghayrah is seen as a protective virtue aligned with divine command, while female ghayrah, if excessive or misplaced, can lead to spiritual deviation.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 124. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
The jealousy of a woman (with co-wives) is heresy, while the jealousy of a man is a part of belief.
